current_answer: Current evidence supports seven distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a public group proposal-and-vote route for the next scene; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end VSA queue-and-playout route; FastVideo has local FastH3 clip paths; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining an unattended dense FastH3 channel at 22.1 fps through 448×448 output, prequeued prompts, and retimed playout; Comfy’s optimized H3 path broadens local access; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate OpenAI-compatible H3 service for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA. A platform-published 5090 benchmark puts one FastH3 Preview v1 path at 55 seconds for 15.08 seconds of 480×640 output and 126 seconds at 768×1024, under its stated hot-job boundary. That is a faster clip-review route, not playback-rate generation. FastH3 8-Step V2 remains a disputed Comfy workflow: FastVideo and the current official Comfy text-to-video template say T2AV only, while the paired official image-to-video template says it accepts first/last-frame FL2VA. A new community report on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S says a 243-frame 768×1344 V2 run completed in 33 minutes 9 seconds; that is a native-canvas local render lead, not a live route.

catalogue_card.question: Does FastH3 V2 get fast on a local iGPU?
catalogue_card.text: One detailed Radeon report says the native 768×1344 V2 route took 33 minutes for about 10 seconds. The catch is the canvas: below a stated token threshold, the sparse path did not help. This is a reproduction lead, not live video.

summary: A new community report gives FastH3 8-Step V2 a condition-rich Radeon route: Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, 128 GB unified memory, ComfyUI v0.36.0, and a 243-frame 768×1344 run reported at 33 minutes 9 seconds.
At 24 fps, 243 frames are about 10.1 seconds. The source-reported native-canvas run is therefore about 196 wall-clock seconds per output second, not a live or playback-rate result.
The author says the VSA path stayed dense below a stated 12,288-token threshold, so the smaller 640×384 case did not gain from FastH3. Canvas and attention path belong beside every speed claim.

FastH3 V2 input scope is still disputed: FastVideo and the current official ComfyUI text-to-video template say T2AV only, while the paired official image-to-video template says first/last-frame FL2VA is supported.
uncertainty: The Radeon 8060S FastH3 V2 timing is one community author’s self-report on a stated Windows ROCm / ComfyUI v0.36.0 setup. The pool did not reproduce it; it does not establish FL2VA, quality, cost, reliability, or a general consumer-GPU baseline.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on the FastH3 8-Step V2 input scope. The pool did not run either T2VA or FL2VA, or measure quality, time, hardware fit, price, queueing, or failures.

Sogni is reporting its own controlled platform benchmark for FastH3 Preview v1, not the newer 8-Step V2 package. The pool did not reproduce it, inspect the worker image, price a Spark, or audit quality, queueing, cold startup, retries, or delivery.
The one-RTX-5090 FastH3 channel is a community project’s one-machine self-report; the pool has not run or independently audited it, and its downloadable files are access-gated.
Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
Yoroll’s YoLive control loop and H3 Superfast timing are company launch claims; the pool did not observe a live vote, measure end-to-end response, or independently reproduce the eight-B200 result.

vLLM-Omni’s H3 serving and four-B300 result are maintainer documentation for one warmed full-H3 FL2VA workload; the pool has not operated it or measured cost, quality, queueing, failure behavior, or client-to-visible latency.
freshness_note: Checked 21 September 2026. A new community benchmark provides a condition-rich FastH3 V2 native-canvas run on a Radeon iGPU, while a direct check of FastVideo and the paired ComfyUI templates leaves FL2VA disputed. The pool did not run the route.
